digest.headline: Sensex rebounds 315 points but Nifty logs a seventh weekly loss; Brent near $100, US jobs data soft.

points.t: Sensex rebounded 315 points to 73,895.74, but Nifty logged its seventh straight weekly loss (another report counts eight).
points.why: Persistent weekly losses show foreign flows, crude and yields are still weighing on Indian equities; the two reports differ on the count.

points.t: Brent was reported above $100 and also back below $100 after G7 and European diesel stock release reports, while dated Brent was said to be above $120.
points.why: Crude near $100 widens India's import bill and feeds inflation, touching oil marketers, aviation and paints; the headlines conflict on which side of $100 Brent closed.

points.t: Morgan Stanley raised its Brent forecasts on a slow Mid-East recovery, and the IEA outlook was upended by the Iran war.
points.why: Higher oil forecasts keep crude the main macro driver for India's inflation and rupee.

points.t: US jobs data was soft, with hiring reported at 29,000, and Wall Street rose with the Nasdaq leading as rate-hike bets cooled.
points.why: Softer rate-hike expectations can ease pressure on foreign flows into India, though it is a US-yield driver rather than a domestic one.

points.t: Treasury yields stayed near a two-decade high and bonds resumed selling after the jobs report, while the dollar fell.
points.why: High US yields pull money away from emerging markets like India; the dollar's dip is a partial offset for the rupee.

points.t: India's forex reserves fell $18.3 bn as the RBI stepped in to defend the rupee, and one report says RBI forex curbs caused $500 mn of losses for Indian banks.
points.why: Rupee defence drains reserves and touches banks, and SBI Research flags rupee and inflation risks for the October MPC.

points.t: FII selling kept Indian stocks under pressure, with brokerages flagging crude and global yields as key risks.
points.why: Foreign flows, crude and yields are the three drivers named together, weighing on large-cap indices.

points.t: A US official said an India-US trade deal is near its end but not imminent, with tariffs and sticking points unresolved.
points.why: No quick deal means tariff uncertainty continues for export-linked sectors.

watch: RBI's October MPC meeting (SBI Research flags inflation and rupee risks; date not given in the headlines)
